signal_rationale.delta: The latest available editions focused on AI productivity/valuation, cross-asset stress and energy security. This issue adds a distinct physical-trade signal: Chinese iron-ore imports are rising while steel and pig-iron output fall, with port inventories and exporter receipts showing where the adjustment is being absorbed.
signal_rationale.evidence: GACC-derived imports +3.1% y/y Jan–Oct; NBS crude steel −2.8%, pig iron −3.1%; SteelHome port inventory +1.16 Mt w/w; Brazil iron-ore export value −27.6% y/y; Port Hedland iron-ore exports −4% y/y; SimFer shipped 2.2 Mt in H1.
signal_rationale.scale_path: China’s procurement and stock management affect seaborne ore prices; Brazil and Australia transmit price changes through export receipts; Guinea’s rail-port corridor adds future supply while its fiscal institutions remain in process.
signal_rationale.transmission: Steel margins and hot-metal output → procurement and inventories → benchmark ore prices and unit values → exporter cash flow, tax receipts and marginal infrastructure finance; energy and freight costs affect delivered costs in parallel.
signal_rationale.falsifier: A sustained decline in port and mill inventories together with rising hot-metal output and improving steel margins would weaken the inventory-led adjustment thesis.

key_constraints: Global October steel production was not yet released at the 06:20 BRT cut-off; September is the latest complete global comparison.
The port-stock figure is a SteelHome industry survey, not a complete official inventory census.
Ore imports and steel output are not directly comparable because of grades, domestic ore, stock changes and shipment timing.
Brazil product-level export values are calculated from MDIC Comex Stat NCM 2601 data.
The latest comparable global credit-spread observation was not available at the cut-off; ECB risk statements are qualitative.
Guinea’s sovereign-fund law was still in a ratification process; no capitalization or operational status was established.

en.title: Ore keeps arriving while steel cools: China shifts the adjustment to inventories and exporters
en.deck: Chinese iron-ore imports rose 3.1% in January–October while crude-steel output fell 2.8%; inventories, margins and new export corridors now determine how the adjustment reaches producers.
en.regime: China’s steel chain is contracting while iron-ore inflows remain resilient; inventories and export receipts are absorbing the mismatch.
en.key_risk: A deeper Chinese steel-demand contraction coinciding with new seaborne supply would compress exporter prices and project cash flows.
